title: Rigveda 10.190: Cosmic order and creation (Aghamarshana)
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.190: Cosmic order and creation (Aghamarshana): Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.190 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to Tapas. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 154v-155r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.190.1-3 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 48); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 155r
translation.original_text:
1ṛ̱taṁ ca̍ sa̱tyaṁ cā̱bhī̍ddhā̱t tapa̱so 'dhy a̍jāyata | tato̱ rātry a̍jāyata̱ tata̍ḥ samu̱dro a̍rṇa̱vaḥ ||
2sa̱mu̱drād a̍rṇa̱vād adhi̍ saṁvatsa̱ro a̍jāyata | a̱ho̱rā̱trāṇi̍ vi̱dadha̱d viśva̍sya miṣa̱to va̱śī ||
3sū̱ryā̱ca̱ndra̱masau̍ dhā̱tā ya̍thāpū̱rvam a̍kalpayat | diva̍ṁ ca pṛthi̱vīṁ cā̱ntari̍kṣa̱m atho̱ sva̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
1FROM Fervour kindled to its height Eternal Law and Truth were born: Thence was the Night produced, and thence the billowy flood of sea arose.
2From that same billowy flood of sea the Year was afterwards produced, Ordainer of the days nights, Lord over all who close the eye.
3Dhatar, the great Creator, then formed in due order Sun and Moon. He formed in order Heaven and Earth, the regions of the air, and light.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 155r (OPenn image 154, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.190.1 ‹-arṇavaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 155v, begins in RV 10.191.4 ‹samānī va ākūtiḥ samānā›. Verses 10.190.1-3 end on this page; 10.190.1 begins on fol. 154v.
